- CA 19-9 = 248 U/mL — markedly elevated, consistent with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in setting of biliary obstruction.  
- MRCP shows extrahepatic bile duct narrowing with abrupt cutoff at the pancreatic head — characteristic of malignant obstruction.  
- CT reveals a 3.2 cm heterogeneously enhancing pancreatic head mass — morphologically typical of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.  
- CT shows SMV encasement — a feature defining borderline resectability and supporting local tumor invasion.  
- No metastases identified on CT — consistent with locally advanced but non-metastatic disease.  
- Explicit exclusion of PSC, choledocholithiasis, and autoimmune pancreatitis in the summary.

[GAPS]  
- No EUS-FNA cytology or biopsy confirmation — tissue diagnosis remains pending.  
- No IgG4 level reported — though autoimmune pancreatitis is stated as excluded clinically/imaging-wise, IgG4 would strengthen that exclusion.  
- No chest CT or PET-CT performed — occult pulmonary or distant metastases cannot be definitively ruled out without dedicated staging imaging.  
- No assessment of carbohydrate antigen 125 (CA-125) or CEA — less specific but occasionally supportive in ambiguous cases (not critical here).  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
